recent_posts.title: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio Code, April releases
recent_posts.summary: GitHub Copilot in VS Code shipped four weekly stable releases (v1.116–v1.119) throughout April and early May 2026. Key additions include semantic search across any workspace, a grep-style GitHub repo/org search tool, and an experimental /chronicle feature that lets you query your own chat history. Token usage is reduced via smarter prompt caching and deferred tool loading. Agents now show inline diffs in chat, can read/write to open terminals, and share live browser tabs as context. Bring-your-own-key support expands to Copilot Business and Enterprise, allowing teams to connect OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, OpenRouter, and local models like Ollama. Copilot CLI sessions can be monitored and steered remotely from GitHub.com or the mobile app, and agent debug logs now persist across sessions.

recent_posts.title: Deprecation notice: code_scanning_upload field will be removed from rate_limit API endpoint
recent_posts.summary: GitHub is removing the `code_scanning_upload` field from the rate_limit REST API endpoint response on May 19, 2026. The field was misleading because it shared the same limit pool as the `core` category, causing confusion about rate limit status. Developers who parse the `/rate_limit` endpoint and reference this field must update their code before that date. The `core` rate limit will continue to govern code scanning uploads with no replacement field needed.

recent_posts.title: Dependency scanning with GitHub MCP Server is in public preview
recent_posts.summary: GitHub MCP Server now includes dependency vulnerability scanning via a new Dependabot toolset, currently in public preview. It allows AI coding agents in MCP-compatible IDEs to scan code changes for vulnerable dependencies before committing or opening a pull request. The toolset queries the GitHub Advisory Database and returns affected packages, severity levels, and recommended fixed versions. An optional advanced-security plugin provides a more tailored experience. Available for repositories with Dependabot alerts enabled, with setup instructions for GitHub Copilot CLI and VS Code.

recent_posts.title: Upcoming deprecation of GPT-5.2 and GPT-5.2-Codex
recent_posts.summary: GitHub is deprecating GPT-5.2 and GPT-5.2-Codex across all GitHub Copilot experiences on June 1st, 2026. GPT-5.5 is the suggested replacement for GPT-5.2, and GPT-5.3-Codex replaces GPT-5.2-Codex. Copilot Enterprise administrators need to enable access to alternative models via model policies in Copilot settings. No action is required to remove deprecated models after the deprecation date.

recent_posts.title: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio — April update
recent_posts.summary: The April 2026 GitHub Copilot update for Visual Studio focuses on agentic workflows. Key additions include cloud agent sessions launchable directly from the IDE (automatically creating GitHub issues and PRs), user-level custom agent definitions stored in a profile directory, expanded agent skill discovery paths, and a new Debugger agent that reproduces bugs from GitHub/Azure DevOps issues and suggests fixes via live runtime execution. Other updates include customizable Copilot keyboard shortcuts, a new chat history panel, generally available C++ code editing tools for agent mode, and auto-decoding in the text visualizer.

recent_posts.title: Copilot Student GPT-5.3-Codex removal from model picker
recent_posts.summary: GitHub is removing GPT-5.3-Codex from the manual model picker in the Copilot Student plan. The model remains accessible via auto model selection, which automatically routes requests to the best-fit model. This change is part of temporary reliability and performance measures across Copilot Individual plans as GitHub prepares for a broader shift to usage-based billing.

recent_posts.title: GitHub Copilot code review will start consuming GitHub Actions minutes on June 1, 2026
recent_posts.summary: Starting June 1, 2026, GitHub Copilot code review will consume GitHub Actions minutes in addition to AI Credits under the new usage-based billing model. This affects private repositories across all Copilot plans (Pro, Pro+, Business, Enterprise). Public repositories remain unaffected. Teams are advised to review their current Actions usage, set appropriate budgets, and inform billing administrators ahead of the change.

recent_posts.title: Copilot cloud agent starts 20% faster with Actions custom images
recent_posts.summary: GitHub Copilot cloud agent now starts over 20% faster due to optimized runner environments built with GitHub Actions custom images. When an issue is assigned to Copilot, a task is started from the Agents tab, or @copilot is mentioned in a PR, the prebuilt custom image reduces startup overhead significantly. This follows a 50% startup improvement shipped in March, continuing to shorten the feedback loop for AI-assisted coding workflows.

recent_posts.title: Inline agent mode in preview and more in GitHub Copilot for JetBrains IDEs
recent_posts.summary: GitHub Copilot for JetBrains IDEs receives several new features: inline agent mode is now in public preview, bringing agent capabilities directly into the inline chat experience without switching to the chat panel. Next Edit Suggestions gains inline edit previews and far-away edit navigation. A new global auto-approve setting lets users automatically approve all tool calls across workspaces, with granular controls for terminal commands and file edits. The update also includes UX improvements like automatic chat context reset, better chat history rendering, and various stability fixes.

recent_posts.title: Notice about upcoming new format for GitHub App installation tokens
recent_posts.summary: GitHub is rolling out a new format for GitHub App installation tokens starting April 27, 2026. The new stateless token format changes from a fixed 40-character string to a longer JWT-based format (~520 characters, variable length) with the pattern ghs_APPID_JWT. The rollout is staged: first-party integrations and GitHub Actions GITHUB_TOKEN are updated April 27 through mid-May, followed by all GitHub App installation tokens through late June. Developers should ensure their apps treat tokens as opaque strings, remove any hardcoded length checks or regex patterns like ghs_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}, and ensure database columns can store at least 520 characters. The change applies to GitHub Enterprise Cloud and Data Residency but not GitHub Enterprise Server.
